ordered_diagnoses: Surgical site recurrence of thyroid cancer

facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s presented with swelling of the manubrium
12 years after resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe through a midline sternotomy approach
The swelling was slightly tender and had increased in size markedly over the month prior to presentation
Swelling noted over the manubrium, which was slightly tender
lytic lesion replacing the manubrium measuring 2.7 × 4.4 × 5.8 cm
residual right goiter
The posterior aspect is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Revealed follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion
Hematoxylin-eosin stained specimens showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae
previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter 12 years ago

concepts.why: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells and the patient's history of thyroid surgery suggest a metastasis from a thyroid primary.
The patient's history of thyroid goiter and the presence of a residual right goiter suggest a recurrence of the condition.

concepts.preferred_label: Surgical site recurrence of thyroid cancer
aliases: Thyroid cancer recurrence at surgical site
concepts.why: The patient's history of thyroid surgery and the presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion suggest a recurrence of thyroid cancer at the surgical site.
The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with proximity to major vessels suggests a bone lesion that may be related to the patient's thyroid condition or surgical history.
The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells and the patient's history of thyroid surgery suggest a thyroid cancer with bone metastasis.
The patient's history of thyroid surgery and the presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion suggest a recurrence of thyroid tissue in the postoperative thyroid bed.

rationales.F05: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium is highly suggestive of bone metastasis, which is a characteristic of thyroid cancer with bone metastasis.
rationales.F08: Follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion suggest a connection between the two, which is consistent with thyroid metastasis to bone or recurrent thyroid goiter.
rationales.F09: Thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae is a characteristic feature of thyroid cancer with bone metastasis.
